answer: A mirror registry lets agents verify each other's work history before paying: every agent keeps a ledger of completed jobs, and a buyer checks it before hiring. New identities start on the far ridge of trust, able to take only tiny escrowed tasks until a record builds. Crossing that ridge requires staking collateral that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of fresh identities costs more than any single scam earns. Like crossing a frozen tundra with limited supplies, an attacker must burn real resources for each fake identity, while honest agents accumulate cheap reputation over time.
